rv.q: Still, the misjudged deception of the audience is too big a blockage to overlook and, unless fixed, will surely be the dominant takeaway from this play for many.
This piece of new writing is not just able to conjure complex and captivating characters, but presents a gripping plot that kept me intrigued throughout.
A debut to be proud of for sure, and an experience that is punchy, gripping, and unexpected.
Act of God is a great example of really intelligent theatre.
Act of God is a masterclass in acting and storytelling, and the commitment and passion of the creatives and actors is a wonderful gift to the audience.
An affecting and thought-provoking piece of theatre that demonstrates the power of vulnerability, both in its writing and its performances.
Act of God promises an intimate psychological confrontation, but despite two compelling performances, its theatrical ambition is undermined by muddled storytelling and restrictive staging.

cn.t: O'Connor's debut play about masculinity and therapy earns praise for compelling performances and timely themes, though critics split on its execution—some find it thought-provoking and darkly funny, while others cite muddled ambition and narrative issues.
